ops.content: The brain daemon restart protocol now routes through `launchctl kickstart -k` rather than a direct Popen spawn. When a restart is needed, the caller invokes `launchctl kickstart -k gui/<UID>/com.brain.daemon` (or the relevant service label), which causes launchd to tear down the existing job and immediately relaunch it under launchd supervision. This ensures the daemon inherits the correct environment, respects the launchd plist configuration, and is automatically re-supervised after the restart. The old Popen-based approach is no longer used and should not be reintroduced.

ops.title: WAL checkpoint starvation under parallel sessions
ops.content: When two sessions write concurrently, the TRUNCATE checkpoint starves; symptom is an ever-growing -wal file.

connect_to.title: e5f6a7b8
connect_to.why: Checkpoint starvation is a direct downstream effect of writer-slot contention: when the WAL writer slot is monopolized by competing sessions, the TRUNCATE checkpoint cannot acquire the exclusive lock it needs, causing the -wal file to grow unboundedly.
